component: HOME phase 1 (Ord. 20231207-001): up to 3 dwelling units per lot, including tiny homes
coverage: Citywide, lots zoned SF-1, SF-2 and SF-3
coding_notes: effective_date is the date the city began accepting applications (2024-02-05); the city page gives no separate effective date. Also removes the primary/secondary distinction and the accessory-apartment and guest-house use categories (ADUs become 2- and 3-unit uses), and the limit on unrelated adults. Two- and three-unit uses: 40% building coverage, 45% impervious cover. FAR tiers by unit count not coded (the ordinance text was not read; not on the city summary page). Single-family use stays under Subchapter F (McMansion). Parking: see TX-4805000-parking-2023. Second coder (2026-10-18): applications-open date confirmed as the start date. Cap of 3 confirmed by the second coder from the city's Phase 1 summary (up to three housing units, including tiny homes, on SF-1/SF-2/SF-3; applies only to duplex, two-unit and three-unit residential uses; single-family use stays under Subchapter F). The city's note that lots created before 2025-06-16 with no more than four units need no drainage review is a later drainage rule, not a HOME unit cap. Building coverage 40% and impervious cover 45% for these uses in all districts (impervious cover up from the pre-HOME SF-1 limit); garages and carports count toward both. Building Official policy memo PM2024-0002 (2024-04-29) confirms the ordinance created a 'three-unit residential' use (three detached units, a unit plus a duplex, or one attached triplex) and, from 2024-04-29, lets triplexes be reviewed under the International Residential Code instead of the IBC when site-plan exempt, at most 3 stories and sprinklered (a cost-lowering implementation step, not coded as its own row).

component: HOME phase 2 (Ord. 20240516-006): small-lot single-family, one unit on lots of at least 1,800 sq ft (was 5,750)
coverage: SF-1, SF-2, SF-3 lots outside the Wildland-Urban Interface and Uprooted Report areas
coding_notes: effective_date is when applications were first accepted. Lots 1,800 to <5,750 sq ft; impervious cover follows base zoning; not eligible for the Preservation Bonus. lot_split=True reads the smaller minimum as allowing subdivision into small lots. City HOME summary (second coder, 2026-10-18): small-lot single-family use keeps the base district's impervious cover limit in SF-1/SF-2/SF-3; in SF-4A, building coverage 55% and impervious cover 65%.

component: HOME phase 2 extended to the remaining areas (citywide)
coverage: SF-1, SF-2, SF-3 lots citywide, adding Wildland-Urban Interface and Uprooted Report areas
coding_notes: Same rules as phase 2a; only coverage widens on 2024-11-16 (city page: applications accepted citywide).

component: Citywide elimination of minimum off-street parking requirements

component: Chapter 42 amendment: by-right minimum single-family lot cut from 5,000 to 3,500 sq ft in the urban area; lots down to 1,400 sq ft with compensating open space or performance standards
coverage: Urban area (inside Loop 610)
coding_notes: Adopted 1998, took effect 1999 (Regulatory Review); exact day not found, effective_date coded as 1999-01-01 (year precision only). parking: a parking space required for larger ADUs
coverage: Citywide

component: SB 15 (2025): new single-family tracts of 5+ acres with no recorded plat cannot be required to have lots over 3,000 sq ft (30 ft wide, 75 ft deep); small lots (<=4,000 sq ft) get caps on setbacks, parking, open space and stories
parking: small lots: no covered or off-site parking, at most 1 space per unit
coverage: Cities over 150,000 people wholly or partly in a county over 300,000; unplatted tracts of 5 acres or more zoned single-family; excludes land near airports and military bases
coding_notes: Signed 2025-06-20 (adoption_date = signature). Covers Austin, Houston, San Antonio, Dallas, Fort Worth and other large cities, but only new subdivisions of 5+ acres: little effect on infill. Setbacks capped at 15 ft front, 10 ft back, 5 ft side; open space/permeable cap 30%; must allow 3 stories. HOA and deed restrictions still apply. parking_min_per_unit is the cap on what a city may require.

component: SB 840 (2025): multifamily and mixed-use allowed by right in zones that allow office, commercial, retail or warehouse use; commercial-to-residential conversions

component: SB 1883 (2025): impact fees need a two-thirds council vote, an independent audit before increases, and cannot rise again for 3 years; AG may sue

component: HOME phase 1 (Ord. 20231207-001): second and third homes on SF-1, SF-2 and SF-3 lots as two- and three-unit residential uses; the secondary-apartment use, ADU maximum size and 10 ft separation removed

Must connect to the main house's utilities; at most 3 occupants; the owner may not take rent for the unit they occupy. Parking: the report says parking rules exist (parking behind the front yard) but no space count, so parking is left blank. FLAG for second coder: sanantonio.gov refused the connection and municode returns 403; check §35-371 history notes.

component: No by-right ADU: a rentable ADU needs a Board of Adjustment special exception (owner occupancy deed restriction) or a neighborhood ADU overlay rezoning (Ords. 30930, 30931); a non-rental 'additional dwelling unit' also needs a special exception
coverage: Single-family districts (R-1ac(A) to R-5(A)); a board case or an overlay rezoning is needed
coding_notes: NO ADU RULE (adus_per_lot = 0): the city ADU page says ADUs 'are not allowed to be built by right in most cases'. Routes: §51A-4.209(b)(6)(E) board special exception (non-rental, deed-restricted; or rentable with an owner-occupancy deed restriction and possible extra parking) and the §51A-4.510(c) ADU overlay (neighborhood petition, CPC and Council). Rentable terms where granted: 700 sq ft or 25% of the main house, whichever is greater; one parking space unless within 1,200 ft of a DART stop. 2 rentable ADUs granted 2018-2020. Framework adopted 2018-06-27 (Ords. 30930/30931, from the city page's file names; effective date not found, coded as the adoption date). Before 2018 only the non-rental special exception existed (adoption date not found). The 2020 by-right proposal (DCA190-007) was held by ZOAC on 2020-10-01 and suspended; no by-right ordinance found through the 2026-05-19 board minutes. FLAG for second coder: §51A-4.209 and §51A-4.510 on amlegal returned 403.

coverage: One-family districts A-2.5A, A-43, A-21, A-10, A-7.5, A-5, AR
coding_notes: NO ADU RULE (adus_per_lot = 0): city council presentation (2024-04-02, slide 10): in A-2.5A, A-43, A-21, A-10, A-7.5, A-5 and AR an accessory dwelling unit is allowed 'when not rented or used as a separate residence' and prohibited when rented or used as one, so it is not a rentable ADU. coverage: All residential (R) and apartment (A) districts, lots with a single-family house; detailed site plan approval in special purpose districts
coding_notes: Ordinance text from the 2011 council agendas (introduced 2011-03-29, on the 2011-04-19 agenda): 'permitted accessory use (A) in all residential (R) and apartment (A) zoning districts'; owner must occupy the principal unit or the ADU. component: UDC (Ord. 14-039): 'secondary living unit' only for family members or relatives and never rented or leased; by right in RE, RS-20, RS-15 and VG, SUP in RS-7.2, RS-5 and RM-12; garage apartments not in single-family districts
coverage: Single-family districts RE, RS-20, RS-15 (by right) and RS-7.2, RS-5 (SUP); family members only

component: Backyard cottages (Zoning Ordinance §15.1800) extended from the Estate Development district to most residential districts: owner occupancy, one extra parking space, 6,000 sq ft minimum lot

One unit must be owner-occupied, either may be rented long term; 6,000 sq ft minimum lot; one extra parking space. The 2024 diagnostic report calls cottages 'by-right in most residential districts'. coding_notes: NO ADU RULE (adus_per_lot = 0): Land Development Code §24-65.3 (R-1): 'Only one (1) dwelling per lot' (as amended by Ord. 92-0-75, 1992-04-06); §24-65.9 (R-1B, Ord. 2023-O-055): one single-family dwelling per lot; §24-65.6 (R-1-MH): one unit per lot. coverage: Single-family districts (SUP case by case)
